question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse checks during an initial trauma assessment?

options.A: Pain assessment
options.B: Airway management
options.C: Wound dressing
options.D: Checking blood pressure

explanation: Think ABCs! Keeping the airway open is always step one because a blocked airway causes a patient to deteriorate the fastest. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h3)

question: How does time-driven activity-based costing make hospital budgeting better?

options.A: By calculating costs strictly at the end of each fiscal year
options.B: By measuring the exact time spent on specific clinical activities
options.C: By ignoring staff salaries and focusing only on medical equipment
options.D: By assuming all hospital stays cost the exact same amount

explanation: This method looks at how many minutes tasks actually take, giving a super accurate picture of what care really costs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: A medical journal uses little numbers in the text that match a numbered list at the end. Which style is this?

options.A: Harvard style
options.B: Chicago style
options.C: APA style
options.D: Vancouver style

explanation: Correct! Vancouver style uses numbers in the text to point straight to the numbered sources at the back. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T7#GNS217_U3_T7_h4)

question: What major feature separates fungi and parasites from bacteria?

options.A: They possess viral capsids instead of cell walls
options.B: They can only survive without oxygen
options.C: They are eukaryotic with a true nucleus
options.D: They lack any form of genetic material

explanation: Unlike bacteria (which are simple prokaryotes), fungi and parasites are eukaryotes—meaning their cells have a proper, organized nucleus, just like human cells do. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why does a lack of estrogen raise the risk of osteoporosis in older women?

options.A: Estrogen directly weakens muscle attachments to bones
options.B: Estrogen normally promotes bone formation and inhibits bone breakdown
options.C: Estrogen stops the absorption of vitamin D in the gut
options.D: Estrogen causes the kidneys to excrete all dietary calcium

explanation: Estrogen acts like a shield for bones by slowing down bone breakdown. Without it, bones can lose their density faster. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T15#GNS121_U5_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a nursing management plan after it has been implemented?

options.A: To hide mistakes from hospital accreditation boards
options.B: To check if the plan achieved its intended goals and outcomes
options.C: To increase the workload for junior nursing students
options.D: To immediately penalize staff who questioned the new policy

explanation: Evaluation determines whether the implemented plan actually solved the problem or reached the target goal. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h7)

question: How does the speed and predictability of rectal absorption generally compare to intravenous injection?

options.A: Rectal absorption is always faster and more exact
options.B: Rectal absorption is usually more erratic and slower
options.C: Rectal drugs never enter the bloodstream at all
options.D: Both methods absorb at the exact same rate

explanation: Intravenous drugs go straight into the bloodstream instantly, whereas rectal drugs must dissolve and cross a membrane first. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h4)

question: What is a clear sign that an expectorant is working successfully?

options.A: The cough becomes more productive and brings up phlegm easily
options.B: The patient develops a high fever and chills overnight
options.C: The cough stops completely within ten minutes of the first dose
options.D: The lung sounds change from clear to heavy coarse crackles

explanation: You got it! Success means the patient can finally clear out that gunk easily instead of having a tight, dry, miserable chest. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which major artery brings the main blood supply to the external male genitalia?

options.A: Common iliac artery
options.B: Internal pudendal artery
options.C: Renal artery
options.D: Femoral artery

explanation: The internal pudendal artery is the main highway delivering rich, oxygenated blood straight to the structures of the penis and scrotum. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T1#GNS121_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does doing night shifts and changing schedules over and over affect a theatre nurse?

options.A: It makes your relationship with doctors and colleagues stronger
options.B: It messes up your sleep, leaving you tired and less alert
options.C: It completely stops any muscle or joint aches
options.D: It balances out your body clock and boosts immunity

explanation: Constantly switching your sleep routine fights against your body's natural clock, making you extra tired and more prone to mistakes. Rest when you can! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T12#GNS123_U5_T12_h5)

question: Which symptom helps you tell the difference between simple breast engorgement and mastitis?

options.A: Hardness and tenderness in both breasts
options.B: Tingling sensation during the let-down reflex
options.C: Leaking of colostrum before the baby feeds
options.D: Presence of fever and systemic flu-like symptoms

explanation: Mastitis is an infection, so it usually comes with a fever and body aches (systemic signs), whereas normal engorgement just makes the breasts heavy and sore without making you feel generally sick. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which of these is a direct health consequence of long-term undernutrition?

options.A: Abnormally elevated blood pressure readings
options.B: Rapid development of metabolic syndrome and obesity
options.C: Severe toxicity from excess fat-soluble vitamins
options.D: Weakened immune response and increased infection risk

explanation: Without enough nutrients, the body's defense cells can't fight off germs properly, leaving room for infections. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h6)

question: What is the main difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: If they come from plant or animal sources
options.B: How fast they dissolve in the bloodstream
options.C: The total amount the body requires daily
options.D: Whether they can provide energy to the body

explanation: You got it! Macro means large (needed in grams), while micro means small (needed in tiny milligram or microgram amounts). [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h3)

question: What is the easiest and most reliable way to track rapid fluid loss in a patient with diarrhoea?

options.A: Daily body weight measurements
options.B: Body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Changes in skin color on the face
options.D: Total number of hours slept per night

explanation: Weight drops fast when you lose body water. Hopping on the scale daily is one of the best ways to catch dangerous dehydration early. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: When a nurse visits a family's home to care for an infant, why is it helpful to view yourself as a 'guest'?

options.A: To respect the family's home environment and autonomy
options.B: To prevent the nurse from providing direct physical care
options.C: Because family members must supervise every nursing task
options.D: Because home nurses have fewer legal responsibilities

explanation: You got it! Walking into someone's home means respecting their private space, culture, and routines. It's the best way to build real trust. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h1)

question: A stroke patient is having trouble swallowing food safely and speaks with slurred words. Who should you call first?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Medical social worker
options.C: Orthopedic surgeon
options.D: Dietitian

explanation: You got it! Speech-language pathologists are the experts when it comes to sorting out both communication troubles and swallowing (dysphagia) issues. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h3)

question: What is the main goal of a health screening test?

options.A: To provide a definitive and final medical diagnosis
options.B: To replace the need for primary prevention vaccines
options.C: To cure a chronic illness without needing further treatment
options.D: To identify unrecognized disease in apparently healthy people

explanation: Screenings help us catch hidden health issues early in people who feel completely fine, giving them a head start on care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h4)

question: Facing discrimination over a long period of time causes which physical response in the body?

options.A: Enhanced muscle growth and physical strength
options.B: Persistent stress and elevated cortisol levels
options.C: Permanent immunity to common infections
options.D: Immediate decrease in blood pressure

explanation: Discrimination acts as a constant stressor, keeping stress hormones like cortisol high and wearing down a person's health over time. Keep learning! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h5)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for pushing those delicate inner cervical cells outward?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Estrogen is the key player here! High levels of estrogen stimulate the inner cervical cells to grow and push outward onto the surface. Great job remembering your reproductive hormones. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Why must nurses check a patient's liver function before starting a long course of albendazole?

options.A: Healthy liver function prevents worms from entering the bloodstream
options.B: Liver cells store the medication for up to six months
options.C: Hepatic enzymes are needed to activate the drug in the stomach
options.D: The medication is metabolized primarily through the liver

explanation: Brilliant! Because the liver breaks down these drugs, we need to make sure it's healthy enough to handle the workload without causing toxicity. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is a fomite in the context of infection control?

options.A: A specialized mask used for airborne disease isolation
options.B: A living insect that carries parasites to humans
options.C: An inanimate object that can transmit infectious agents
options.D: A chemical spray used to clean hospital floors

explanation: Fomites are non-living surfaces or objects like stethoscopes or tables that hold onto germs and pass them along. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: What is a major logistical problem caused by uncoordinated disaster donations?

options.A: Relief workers spend all their time cooking donated food
options.B: Local markets experience a permanent surplus of luxury vehicles
options.C: Hospitals run out of storage space for monetary funds
options.D: Unwanted goods block transport routes while essential items get stuck

explanation: Sending random unrequested supplies clogs up ports and roads, delaying the delivery of life-saving medical gear. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why should every task on a project checklist be assigned to a specific person?

options.A: To make it easier to fire workers who make minor mistakes
options.B: To ensure only the facility director does any actual work
options.C: To ensure accountability so responsibilities are never neglected
options.D: To prevent team members from communicating with each other

explanation: When everyone is responsible, no one is responsible! Assigning names ensures every important task actually gets done. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h4)

question: Why do modern healthcare programs make sure to involve male partners in reproductive health?

options.A: Men are the only family members who suffer from reproductive infections
options.B: Men often influence household health decisions and resource allocation
options.C: Male involvement completely removes the need for female health education
options.D: Women are legally prohibited from visiting clinics alone

explanation: Great reasoning! Since men often hold the purse strings and make major home decisions in many communities, getting them on board is key to success. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h6)

question: A nurse opens a sterile dressing pack for a patient, but the procedure is cancelled before the pack is touched. What is the best nursing action to minimize waste?

options.A: Place the pack in the general waste bin to save space
options.B: Check hospital policy to see if the unopened sterile pack remains usable
options.C: Send the pack immediately to the hospital incinerator
options.D: Throw the unopened pack straight into the infectious waste bin

explanation: If a sterile barrier is completely intact and unopened, facility guidelines often allow it to remain sterile, preventing needless waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: Why is it so important for frontline ward nurses to be involved when designing new clinical software?

options.A: Hospital accreditation rules legally require nurses to write code
options.B: They are the only staff members trained in computer programming
options.C: They understand actual daily workflows better than remote administrators
options.D: They have extra free time during their shifts to test products

explanation: Spot on! Office administrators don't face the realities of the ward. Frontline nurses know what actually works during a busy shift. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why do health workers draw an epidemic curve on a graph during an outbreak?

options.A: To show the timeline of when cases occurred and track the outbreak's progress
options.B: To prove to international donors that funding was spent wisely
options.C: To measure the physical distance between houses in the village
options.D: To predict exactly what the weather will be like next week

explanation: Brilliant! An epidemic curve turns dates into a picture, helping investigators see when infections started and whether the outbreak is slowing down or growing. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h5)

question: Why is the role of a food handler particularly critical in a hospital environment?

options.A: Hospital patients eat more frequently than people outside
options.B: Hospital kitchens prepare larger quantities of food than standard restaurants
options.C: Hospital patients often have weakened immune systems that make them vulnerable to infections
options.D: Hospital food handlers are required to have medical degrees

explanation: Vulnerable patients in healthcare facilities suffer severe complications from foodborne illnesses that healthy people might overcome easily. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: Why are vital statistics like death registries important for health surveillance?

options.A: They measure the trading volume of the local agricultural market.
options.B: They calculate the daily water supply pressure in the city.
options.C: They help track causes of death and overall population health trends.
options.D: They show which political party won the local government election.

explanation: Death registries give us a big-picture view of what is really killing people in our communities, guiding where public health help is needed most. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h5)

question: Why do government health systems often partner with non-governmental agencies?

options.A: Communities prefer private doctors over public nurses
options.B: Ministries of health do not care about rural populations
options.C: Hospitals lack enough space to store modern medicines
options.D: Government facilities face funding limits and personnel shortages

explanation: You got it! Because budgets and staff numbers can be tight, government agencies often need extra hands to reach every corner of the country. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: A patient with severe salpingitis, high fever, and nonstop vomiting is admitted for IV antibiotics. What is the main reason for hospital admission?

options.A: Need for immediate total removal of both fallopian tubes
options.B: Requirement for daily pelvic ultrasound monitoring at bedside
options.C: Desire to isolate the patient from all household family members
options.D: Inability to tolerate oral medications due to severe nausea

explanation: If a patient can't keep pills down because of vomiting, oral meds won't work. Bringing them in for IV treatment ensures the drugs actually get into their system. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h6)

question: What is the main job of Phase I metabolic reactions?

options.A: To build brand new proteins from scratch inside the bloodstream
options.B: To store extra vitamins inside the liver cells for later use
options.C: To introduce or uncover a polar functional group on the drug molecule
options.D: To attach a large bulky sugar molecule to trap the drug in fat

explanation: Phase I is all about tweaking the drug slightly—adding or exposing a little chemical handle (a polar group) so the body can grab onto it for the next steps. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h3)

question: How does community health nursing mainly differ from bedside hospital nursing?

options.A: The community nurse only prescribes medications for chronic conditions
options.B: The hospital nurse never interacts with people from different towns
options.C: The community nurse focuses on population-wide health promotion and disease prevention
options.D: The community nurse ignores individual family needs completely

explanation: You nailed it! Community nursing is all about stopping sickness before it starts by looking after the health of the entire group. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T1#GNS225_U1_T1_h5)

question: In livestock farming, what do we call a disease that can jump between animals and humans?

options.A: A plant infection caused by heavy rainfall
options.B: A mechanical failure of milking equipment
options.C: An illness that can spread between animals and humans
options.D: A vitamin deficiency found only in farm workers

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections that naturally pass from animals to us. Think of illnesses like bird flu or rabies! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h3)

question: How must controlled substances be stored on a hospital ward?

options.A: In an open metal tray on the main nurses' station desk
options.B: Inside the patient's bedside locker for easy access
options.C: In a double-locked secure cabinet with restricted key access
options.D: Inside the general refrigerator with food items

explanation: Double-locking prevents theft, diversion, and unauthorized access to dangerous drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which of these should you NOT do when planning a community health talk against harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Mocking and condemning traditional cultural heritage
options.B: Partnering with respected local village elders
options.C: Educating parents about blood-borne infection risks
options.D: Promoting safe, non-invasive alternatives for identity

explanation: Spot on! Insulting local culture only makes people defensive. Good public health education is always respectful, kind, and informative. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h7)

question: Why should a nurse manager care about keeping the ward staff motivated?

options.A: It allows the manager to reduce overall nursing salaries
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for hospital policies
options.C: It leads to safer patient care and better staff retention
options.D: It guarantees that nurses will never make charting errors

explanation: You got it! When nurses feel valued and motivated, patients get safer care, and people are much happier staying on the team. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the typical needle length you'll grab for an adult subcutaneous injection?

options.A: 1.5 to 2 inches
options.B: 1 inch to 1.25 inches
options.C: 2 to 3 inches
options.D: 3/8 to 5/8 inch

explanation: Correct! Since subcutaneous injections only need to reach the fat layer, short needles measuring 3/8 to 5/8 of an inch are all it takes. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why are patients who vomit heavily for a long time at high risk for metabolic alkalosis?

options.A: They eat too many alkaline foods while recovering
options.B: Their lungs trap extra carbon dioxide to fix the fluid loss
options.C: Their kidneys completely stop making urine
options.D: They lose large amounts of stomach acid

explanation: Vomiting throws out hydrochloric acid from your stomach, leaving your body with extra base, which pushes your blood pH up into alkalosis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the main objective of the empowerment approach in health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring that government officials make all health decisions for citizens
options.B: Forcing communities to build modern hospitals using their own unpaid labor
options.C: Helping people gain the confidence and skills to take control of their own health
options.D: Relying solely on foreign pharmaceutical donations

explanation: Empowerment focuses on building self-reliance so communities can advocate for their own needs and solve local health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main drawback of the immune response triggered by T-independent antigens?

options.A: They completely prevent any immediate white blood cell activation
options.B: They destroy healthy host tissues alongside invading pathogens
options.C: They fail to create strong long-term immunological memory
options.D: They require months of processing before antibodies appear

explanation: Without T-cells stepping in to help, the body reacts quickly but fails to build long-lasting memory cells for future protection. [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why does the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) have to rely on diffusion to get its nutrients?

options.A: It is made entirely of dead cells.
options.B: It repels blood vessels using keratin.
options.C: It is too thick for capillaries to enter.
options.D: It lacks a direct blood supply.

explanation: Exactly! The epidermis doesn't have its own blood vessels (it's avascular). Because of this, nutrients have to quietly seep up from the dermis living right below it. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h2)

question: When is chemical disinfection most commonly used in a healthcare facility?

options.A: For treating liquid infectious waste and laboratory cultures
options.B: For packaging expired patient food trays
options.C: For disposing of heavy metal surgical instruments
options.D: For processing large wooden crates and office furniture

explanation: Liquid waste and lab cultures are often treated directly with chemical disinfectants to make them safe before they go down the sewer lines. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: Why do doctors test breast cancer tissue for HER2 receptors?

options.A: It tells the doctor exactly how many months the patient has to live
options.B: It prevents the cancer from spreading to the bone marrow
options.C: It proves the patient has a family history of endocrine disorders
options.D: It identifies tumors that may respond to specific HER2-blocking medications

explanation: Finding HER2 helps doctors target the cancer directly with specialized medications that block these specific growth signals. Modern medicine is amazing like that! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to psychiatric follow-up care in Nigeria?

options.A: Zero cultural stigma surrounding mental illness
options.B: Free transportation provided to all patients
options.C: Long distances to health facilities and high medication costs
options.D: An excess of psychiatric hospitals in every village

explanation: Financial strain and distance are major hurdles that prevent patients from attending regular clinic visits in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why is it important for nursing students to understand how healthcare is funded?

options.A: Nurses are directly responsible for collecting hospital revenue
options.B: It explains why some facilities lack basic supplies and equipment
options.C: It is required for writing national health policies
options.D: It determines the specific salary scale for health workers

explanation: You've got this! Knowing where hospital money comes from helps you make sense of the real-world shortages and everyday challenges you will see during clinical postings. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the medical term for painful menstrual cramps caused by trapped blood behind scar tissue?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Amenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Polymenorrhea

explanation: You got it! Dysmenorrhea means painful periods—and the pain becomes severe when scar tissue blocks menstrual blood from flowing out normally. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h3)

question: A nurse ignores a ward medication rule, and the patient gets hurt. What legal problem might this cause?

options.A: The hospital policy automatically protects the nurse from blame
options.B: The legal system ignores internal hospital rules completely
options.C: The policy becomes invalid because a nurse chose not to use it
options.D: The breach of policy can be used as evidence of negligence

explanation: Skipping established safety steps without a good clinical reason makes it much easier to prove a breach of duty if something goes wrong. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h2)

question: Where should a patient place their body weight when walking with crutches?

options.A: Through the shoulders
options.B: Against the armpits
options.C: Through the hands
options.D: Against the chest wall

explanation: Always push through the hands, not the armpits! Putting weight in the armpits can damage important nerves and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h6)

question: What should a nurse do if a sound-minded patient at home refuses treatment?

options.A: Respect the refusal and document the discussion thoroughly
options.B: Call the police to arrest the family members
options.C: Force the patient to take the treatment immediately
options.D: Ignore the refusal and administer the drug secretly

explanation: Exactly right! Competent patients have every right to decide what happens to their bodies, including saying no to treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which approach is most appropriate during an open disclosure conversation with an affected family?

options.A: Insisting that the hospital bears no responsibility whatsoever for the event
options.B: Speculating wildly about who was sleeping on duty when the error occurred
options.C: Avoiding eye contact and handing them an administrative pamphlet
options.D: Expressing genuine sorrow for the outcome and outlining steps for investigation

explanation: Families deserve empathy, sorrow for their suffering, and assurance that a thorough investigation is underway. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h5)

question: Where is the normal point of maximal impulse (PMI) located on a healthy adult chest?

options.A: Second intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: Third intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: Seventh intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
options.D: Fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line

explanation: You'll usually find the normal PMI right at the fifth intercostal space along the left midclavicular line. Excellent clinical landmark! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: If a patient catches an infection later in life that weakens their immune system, what is this called?

options.A: Primary hypersensitivity
options.B: Innate immune enhancement
options.C: Secondary immunodeficiency
options.D: Active artificial immunity

explanation: When the immune system becomes weak due to later-life factors like infections, environment, or medications, we call it a secondary immunodeficiency. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h7)

question: A nurse is sent to a remote village with no motorable roads or clinic. What kind of situation is this?

options.A: Single parents with plenty of cash
options.B: Internally displaced persons waiting for homes
options.C: Rural families facing geographic and infrastructure challenges
options.D: Urban rich families taking a break from business

explanation: Spot on! Isolated villages struggle because bad roads and lack of basic infrastructure make it really hard to reach standard healthcare. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h3)

question: Why is suddenly stopping long-term steroid therapy so dangerous (leading to an addisonian crisis)?

options.A: The kidneys start excreting all remaining sodium and water within minutes
options.B: The sudden lack of steroids causes a massive uncontrolled surge of white blood cells
options.C: The adrenal glands have atrophied and cannot immediately produce natural cortisol
options.D: The liver immediately stops filtering toxins out of the circulating bloodstream

explanation: Since the adrenal glands were resting while taking synthetic pills, they can't instantly wake up and make natural cortisol when you stop abruptly. This causes a dangerous drop in blood pressure and shock. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h7)

question: What severe childhood malnutrition condition can happen when protein foods are restricted for too long?

options.A: Hypertension and stroke
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Kwashiorkor or marasmus

explanation: When a child's diet lacks proper protein and calories over time due to strict taboos, it sadly paves the way for protein-energy malnutrition like kwashiorkor. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h5)

question: When is the best time to put a newborn baby to the breast for the very first time?

options.A: Only when the mother's milk turns white
options.B: After twenty-four hours of observation
options.C: Within the first hour after birth
options.D: Once the baby cries continuously

explanation: You nailed it! Starting breastfeeding within that first hour helps boost milk flow and gives the baby that precious, protective colostrum. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h3)

question: What is the most widely accepted theory for how endometrial tissue ends up outside the uterus?

options.A: Retrograde menstruation
options.B: Lymphatic vessel spread
options.C: Bacterial contamination
options.D: Direct muscular invasion

explanation: Retrograde menstruation means some menstrual flow travels backward through the fallopian tubes, carrying healthy uterine lining cells out into the pelvic cavity. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is the main difference between a descriptive and an analytical epidemiological study?

options.A: Analytical studies test hypotheses about causes, while descriptive studies only organize basic health data
options.B: Analytical studies are only conducted in hospitals, while descriptive studies happen outdoors
options.C: Descriptive studies require laboratory tests, while analytical studies only use interviews
options.D: Descriptive studies cost more money to run than analytical studies

explanation: You got it! Descriptive research tells us the 'what, where, and when', while analytical research digs deeper to find the 'why'. Keep going! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h4)

question: In public health, what are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Immunity, infection, and recovery
options.B: Vector, carrier, and reservoir
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Host, agent, and environment

question: Why must rescue workers stabilize a victim before moving them to a hospital?

question: How is a nursing audit different from a general staff performance appraisal?

question: Which of these is a core duty of a psychiatric nurse in an MHPSS team?

question: A clinic nurse notices a sudden spike in measles cases in the monthly records. What is the best practical step to take?

question: Why do people call the CPU the 'brain' of the computer?

question: Which ethical principle are you upholding when you give a patient honest, complete details about a drug's side effects?

question: Why are older adults more likely to experience drug toxicity than younger adults?

question: Why do whole fruits cause a slower, safer rise in blood sugar than fruit juices?

question: A patient on hydrochlorothiazide complains of feeling very weak and dizzy. What is your best nursing action?

question: How does nursing in a Rapid Response Center differ from regular hospital ward nursing?

question: Why do modern nurses need to understand a bit of health economics?

question: Which diagnostic test specifically records the electrical activity of the brain?

question: Why is a mother's nutrition directly linked to her baby's health?

question: How do oxygen and glucose generally move from the capillary blood into the body tissues?

question: When smooth muscle is getting ready to contract, which protein does calcium bind to?

question: On a standard ECG tracing, what does the QRS complex show us?

question: Why is it important for a nurse to respect local food taboos rather than arguing with patients about them?

question: How does active immunization protect the body against future infections?

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a patient first believe before changing a health habit?

question: In Superior Mesenteric Artery syndrome, what actually squeezes or traps the duodenum?

question: What is the main goal of using descriptive statistics in healthcare?

question: What is the big advantage of a concurrent audit compared to a retrospective one?

question: Which of these is a daily operational duty in a running health clinic?

question: What is the main thing a nurse does when acting as a health advocate?

question: A patient is discouraged because their BMI hasn't budged after starting an exercise routine. What else can you suggest tracking?

options.A: Waist circumference and overall energy levels
options.B: Resting body temperature and pulse rate
options.C: Daily fluid retention and shoe size changes
options.D: Total body height measured twice a week

explanation: Spot on! When starting fitness, patients often swap fat for muscle. Checking waist size and energy levels will often show great progress before the scale moves! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h8)

question: A surgical team accidentally leaves a gauze pack inside a patient's belly during an operation. Which category does this fit into?

options.A: Healthcare-associated infections
options.B: Latent organizational failures
options.C: Diagnostic errors
options.D: Surgical complications

explanation: This falls right under surgical complications. Mistakes like leaving items behind or operating on the wrong site are serious things the surgical team works hard to prevent. [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which brain structure releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to start the reproductive hormone chain?

options.A: The anterior pituitary
options.B: The hypothalamus
options.C: The pineal gland
options.D: The adrenal cortex

explanation: The hypothalamus initiates the hormonal cascade by releasing gonadotropin-releasing hormone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the main goal of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To find out which hospital ward cost the most money
options.B: To collect financial donations from family members
options.C: To monitor exposed individuals and catch new cases early
options.D: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteers

explanation: Well done! Tracking down people who were exposed lets us watch them closely and isolate them before they can spread the illness further. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why must insulin be given as an injection instead of swallowing it as a pill?

options.A: Injections allow insulin to bypass the liver entirely
options.B: Digestive enzymes in the stomach destroy the insulin molecule
options.C: Stomach acid turns insulin into a toxic compound
options.D: Oral pills are absorbed too rapidly to be safe

explanation: Exactly! Insulin is a protein, so the acids and enzymes in your gut would break it down before it ever reached your bloodstream if you swallowed it. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h2)

question: A new mother looks exhausted and tells you she feels totally hopeless weeks after delivery. What should you do first?

options.A: Provide a supportive listening ear and involve family in her care
options.B: Tell her to ignore her feelings and focus entirely on chores
options.C: Leave her alone so she can sleep without any interruptions
options.D: Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately to gain rest

explanation: Start by listening without judgment and bringing her support system on board. Validating her feelings is a great first step toward healing. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h7)

question: What is a common cause of diarrhea when a patient is receiving tube feeds at home?

options.A: Elevating the bed during the feeding
options.B: Keeping the room temperature too warm
options.C: Infusing the formula too rapidly
options.D: Flushing the tube with plain sterile water

explanation: Correct! Pumping formula too fast overwhelms the gut and frequently causes cramps and diarrhea. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is a common reason why busy nurses might resist new quality improvement ideas?

options.A: They lack basic literacy skills required to read medical charts
options.B: They prefer making clinical errors rather than following guidelines
options.C: They are legally barred from participating in hospital management
options.D: They already feel overworked and view changes as extra tasks

explanation: Exactly. When shifts are already heavy and exhausting, any new process can feel like an extra burden unless its value is clearly shown. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h6)

question: A patient is having a rising panic attack at home. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink several cups of strong coffee
options.B: Scold the patient for worrying over unimportant matters
options.C: Leave the patient completely alone in a dark room until they calm down
options.D: Guide the patient through slow, deep breathing exercises

explanation: Brilliant! Slow, steady breaths help lower the heart rate and calm down hyperventilation. Nursing care at its finest! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: To store health insurance billing information for government agencies
options.B: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated tasks
options.C: To store a patient's digital medical history for authorized sharing
options.D: To provide patients with a private diary of their daily symptoms

explanation: An EHR is a digital chart designed primarily to collect and safely share comprehensive patient health information among healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do the autonomic and somatic nervous systems team up to keep you continent?

options.A: Somatic nerves open the bladder neck while autonomic nerves squeeze the outer muscles.
options.B: Autonomic fibers manage involuntary internal muscle tone while somatic fibers control the voluntary outer sphincter.
options.C: Both systems rely entirely on conscious thought to prevent accidental leakage.
options.D: Autonomic nerves stop urine production while somatic nerves pump urine down the tube.

explanation: Brilliant! It's a teamwork effort: involuntary nerves handle the inside muscles automatically, while voluntary nerves let you decide when to use the restroom. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why must nurses assess the mental well-being of people undergoing quarantine?

options.A: Depression causes immediate immunity to infections
options.B: Mental illness stops the incubation period of viruses
options.C: Psychological stress lowers body temperature
options.D: Confinement often leads to anxiety, stress, and frustration

explanation: Being cut off from normal routines and social contact places a heavy psychological toll on individuals in quarantine. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h4)

question: When introducing a new practice to a unit, why is it so helpful to involve local peer champions?

options.A: Peer champions are the only staff members legally allowed to train others
options.B: Local champions work longer hours without extra pay than regular nurses
options.C: Staff trust and follow respected colleagues more readily than distant managers
options.D: Hospital policy requires a peer champion to sign off on every patient chart

explanation: As student nurses, we know we look up to our senior colleagues and trusted peers for guidance. Peer influence is a powerful tool for positive change! [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h4)

question: A doctor orders a pain relief pill marked 'prn'. When should you give this drug?

options.A: Every four hours exactly on the clock
options.B: Only when the patient reports pain
options.C: Twice daily regardless of symptoms
options.D: Right before the patient eats breakfast

explanation: Exactly! 'prn' stands for 'pro re nata', meaning 'as needed'. You give it when the patient's symptoms call for it, like asking for pain relief. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h2)

question: A researcher decides to pick every 5th patient from the clinic register. Which sampling method is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Convenience sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: You nailed it! Going down a list at regular intervals (like every 5th or 10th person) is called systematic sampling. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h3)

question: What is meant by the 'utilization rate' of a healthcare facility?

options.A: How quickly the pharmacy dispenses routine medications
options.B: The total number of chairs in the hospital waiting room
options.C: The monthly electricity bill paid by the clinic
options.D: How often community members actually visit and use the services

explanation: Utilization rate measures the extent to which the target population uses available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: What are the two main hormone types found in combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Prolactin and progestin
options.B: Progesterone and testosterone
options.C: Estrogen and oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen and progestin

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives contain a blend of synthetic estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h1)

question: Why is looking at a trend of vital signs over several hours so much better than just checking a single set of numbers?

options.A: It is required for billing and insurance records
options.B: It proves the machine is working properly
options.C: It shows the direction the patient's health is moving
options.D: It replaces the need for physician physical exams

explanation: Exactly! Tracking numbers over time helps you spot a slow, steady slip in a patient's condition, even if their current numbers still technically look 'normal.' [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h2)

question: During the rainy season, a community health nurse sees more waterborne illnesses. What is the best immediate community action to prioritize?

options.A: Encouraging families to sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets every night
options.B: Advising community members to avoid all physical contact during greetings
options.C: Promoting daily physical exercise to strengthen cardiovascular endurance
options.D: Educating residents on water purification methods like boiling or chlorination

explanation: You got it! Since waterborne diseases spread through contaminated drinking water, making the water safe to drink is the most direct way to stop them. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T4#GNS313_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should a nurse designer limit a health poster to just one or two main actions?

options.A: Health workers do not have time to memorize long lists of instructions.
options.B: Paper becomes too heavy and expensive to distribute easily.
options.C: Government printing presses refuse to print more than two sentences.
options.D: Too many competing messages confuse the audience and dilute the impact.

explanation: Keep it simple! If you put too many instructions on one poster, people get overwhelmed and walk away remembering nothing. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main reason for using a nursing theory in your research?

options.A: To dictate the exact medication dosage a patient must receive
options.B: To replace the need for ethical approval from the hospital board
options.C: To provide a structured framework for examining patient care
options.D: To calculate the monthly budget for the nursing unit

explanation: Theories act like a pair of glasses, helping us look at patient care in an organized and logical way. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the main job of the rehab nurse within the healthcare team?

options.A: Prescribing physical therapy exercises and ordering diagnostic imaging tests
options.B: Reinforcing therapy skills and coordinating daily care around the clock
options.C: Providing formal legal counseling for insurance claims
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries to correct bone deformities

explanation: Nurses are with the patient 24/7. We tie all the therapies together and keep the healing going round the clock. You are the heartbeat of the ward! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why must you always write down the body site (like oral or tympanic) along with the temperature number?

options.A: Different sites use completely different scales like Kelvin
options.B: Electronic health records will lock your chart without it
options.C: Hospital insurance demands the name of the device maker
options.D: Normal body temperature ranges change depending on where you measure it

explanation: Different parts of the body naturally run at slightly different baselines, so knowing the route is vital to read the results correctly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h8)

question: What is a major benefit of using video conferencing for patient follow-up care?

options.A: It bridges geographical gaps for patients in remote areas
options.B: It completely replaces the need for any in-person hospital visits
options.C: It removes all requirements for patient data privacy protection
options.D: It allows nurses to physically change dressings from miles away

explanation: Video tools allow nurses to assess and support patients who live far away without requiring them to travel to the facility. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h3)

question: Where do the best and most practical nursing research questions usually come from?

options.A: Direct observations from everyday bedside clinical practice
options.B: Administrative budget meetings in the hospital boardroom
options.C: Textbooks written over fifty years ago
options.D: Abstract philosophical theories about human behavior

explanation: The ward is a goldmine for research! Everyday things you notice while caring for patients at the bedside spark the most helpful nursing studies. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h5)

question: A patient is admitted to the emergency room with extreme restlessness, high blood pressure, and dilated pupils after taking a street drug. Which substance class is most likely involved?

options.A: Opioids
options.B: Depressants
options.C: Stimulants
options.D: Sedatives

explanation: Stimulants speed up the central nervous system, causing signs like high blood pressure, rapid heart rate, and dilated pupils. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the main public health goal of achieving high herd immunity within a community?

options.A: To guarantee lifelong immunity without booster doses
options.B: To protect vulnerable individuals who cannot receive vaccines
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To completely eliminate all known chronic illnesses

explanation: When most of the population is vaccinated, it creates a protective barrier that stops infectious agents from reaching people who are too young or sick to get vaccinated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: Why are dietary fats considered energy-dense?

options.A: They contain no carbon or hydrogen atoms
options.B: They convert directly into muscle without breakdown
options.C: They are digested much faster than carbs
options.D: They supply more than double the calories per gram compared to carbs or protein

explanation: You've got this! Fats give you nine calories per gram, while proteins and carbs only give four. That means fats pack much more energy into a smaller amount. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: Why do dietitians need to understand human behavior along with food science?

options.A: Food chemistry changes completely based on the patient's mood
options.B: Patients need to feel understood in their cultural and personal habits to follow meal plans
options.C: Biochemical data alone is enough to change eating habits permanently
options.D: Psychological evaluations are legally required before writing a hospital diet

explanation: Knowing the science of food is only half the battle! If a patient's personal or cultural beliefs clash with the diet, they won't be able to follow it. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h1)

question: Why are antibiotics prescribed as part of treatment for some peptic ulcers?

options.A: Directly neutralizing excess hydrochloric acid in the gut
options.B: Blocking histamine receptors on gastric parietal cells
options.C: Coating the stomach wall to prevent physical irritation
options.D: Eradicating Helicobacter pylori bacterial infections

explanation: Many ulcers are caused by a stubborn bacteria called H. pylori. Clearing it out with antibiotics helps the ulcer heal completely. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main goal of infection control when caring for patients right inside their own homes?

options.A: Eliminating all microorganisms from the domestic environment
options.B: Transforming the private home into a sterile hospital room
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment maintenance
options.D: Breaking the chain of infection to protect clients and workers

explanation: Spot on! The big picture in home care is always stopping germs from spreading between you and your patient. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To determine the final retirement pension of the employee
options.B: To establish a baseline health status before job exposure begins
options.C: To diagnose casual community infections like malaria
options.D: To punish workers who have past medical conditions

explanation: A pre-placement check gives us a clear picture of a worker's health before they start a new job, so we can track and protect their health later on. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h4)

question: Which type of germ is the absolute hardest to kill with standard chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Vegetative bacteria
options.B: Enveloped respiratory viruses
options.C: Gram-positive cocci
options.D: Bacterial endospores

explanation: Endospores have built-in super coats that make them amazingly resistant to heat, drying, and harsh chemicals. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h5)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the very beginning of the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Solution
options.B: Situation
options.C: Severity
options.D: Symptoms

explanation: Spot on! In SBAR, the first 'S' is for Situation—a quick summary of what is happening right now that made you call or report. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of home health care?

options.A: To replace traditional long-term nursing home facilities
options.B: To provide permanent 24-hour bedside critical care
options.C: To help patients recover and live independently at home
options.D: To reduce the workload of busy hospital physicians

explanation: Home health services focus on bringing medical and support care to the residence so individuals can manage conditions and recover safely where they live. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: What makes data a 'primary source' in research?

options.A: Data retrieved from older textbooks found in the university library
options.B: Information published in international nursing journals last year
options.C: Patient records stored in the hospital archive from a decade ago
options.D: Information collected firsthand by the researcher for the current study

explanation: Primary data is fresh data you collect yourself right from the source for your own study! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h2)

question: What is the main goal of introducing a new idea for change in healthcare?

options.A: Lowering the salaries of clinical staff
options.B: Increasing the administrative workload of nurses
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital beds
options.D: Improving care delivery and patient outcomes

explanation: We always want our patients to get better! An idea for change is simply a practical way to make nursing care smoother and help patients recover faster. [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do women need to use chemical spermicide along with a diaphragm?

options.A: To lubricate the device for easy insertion
options.B: To immobilize and kill sperm that pass the barrier
options.C: To permanently alter the pH of the cervix
options.D: To prevent the growth of yeast infections

explanation: While the physical cup blocks most sperm, spermicide acts as a backup to kill any little swimmers that might slip past the edges! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h1)

question: Why do mental health issues in displaced populations often get missed during standard medical checks?

options.A: Trauma only affects physical organs and never the nervous system.
options.B: Healthcare workers are legally forbidden from asking about mood.
options.C: Displaced persons do not experience psychological stress.
options.D: Patients frequently present with physical symptoms masking their emotional distress.

explanation: Emotional pain doesn't always look like crying. Often, patients show up with physical complaints like constant headaches, stomach aches, or fatigue when deep down they are dealing with trauma. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h4)

question: Why is the elimination of handwritten nursing notes considered a major safety improvement?

options.A: It makes paper storage rooms completely unnecessary in every hospital
options.B: It allows computers to automatically write the discharge summary for the doctor
options.C: It prevents medication errors caused by misreading unclear handwriting
options.D: It ensures that nurses never make any clinical documentation mistakes

explanation: Clear digital text removes the guesswork and dangerous mistakes that frequently arise from reading messy or faded handwriting on paper charts. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between dyspnoea and tachypnoea?

options.A: Dyspnoea only occurs during sleep, while tachypnoea occurs while awake.
options.B: Dyspnoea is caused by infection, while tachypnoea is caused by anxiety.
options.C: Dyspnoea is a subjective feeling, while tachypnoea is an objective breathing rate.
options.D: Dyspnoea involves low oxygen levels, while tachypnoea involves normal oxygen.

explanation: Dyspnoea is what the patient feels, whereas tachypnoea is simply a counted respiratory rate above normal limits. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which finding is a normal vascular change expected during a routine prenatal checkup?

options.A: Sudden widespread purpura and bruising
options.B: Small spider angiomas on the upper chest
options.C: Painful deep purple nodules on the calves
options.D: Complete absence of blood flow to the fingers

explanation: Spotting small spider-like blood vessels (angiomas) is super common due to extra blood volume and high estrogen during pregnancy. Nothing to worry about! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h3)

question: Why is relying heavily on defense mechanisms for a long time a bad idea?

options.A: It prevents the individual from directly addressing and solving the root problem
options.B: It stops the liver from metabolizing medications properly
options.C: It guarantees the person will develop a permanent personality disorder
options.D: It automatically causes severe physical organ failure

explanation: They give us a quick break from reality, but using them too much means we never actually face or fix what's causing the emotional pain. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h4)

question: If your patient is very thin and malnourished, how might you adjust your subcutaneous technique?

options.A: The injection must be given at a 90-degree angle always
options.B: The medication must be diluted with sterile water first
options.C: A longer needle must be used to reach the fat layer
options.D: A shorter needle and a shallower insertion angle may be needed

explanation: Exactly! Thin patients have less fat padding, so using a shorter needle or a 45-degree angle helps make sure you don't accidentally go straight into the muscle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main ethical goal of triage when a mass disaster happens?

options.A: Saving the most critically ill patient first, regardless of resource consumption.
options.B: Ensuring doctors spend equal amounts of time on every single casualty.
options.C: Providing the greatest good for the greatest number of people using available resources.
options.D: Treating every patient in the exact order they arrived at the hospital.

explanation: Exactly! Disaster triage flips routine care on its head: instead of focusing only on the sickest individual, you focus on saving as many lives as possible with what you have. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the protective protein shell enclosing a virus's genetic material called?

options.A: Flagella
options.B: Spore
options.C: Peptidoglycan
options.D: Capsid

explanation: The capsid serves as armor protecting the fragile viral DNA or RNA. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary role of skeletal muscles during ambulation?

options.A: Contracting to pull bones and create motion
options.B: Sending electrical signals to the brain
options.C: Producing red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.D: Absorbing shock within the joint spaces

explanation: Skeletal muscles shorten and pull on bones across joints to move the body forward during walking. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which medication is standard for stopping seizures in a pregnant woman with eclampsia?

options.A: Sodium bicarbonate
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Calcium gluconate
options.D: Diazepam drops

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the magic word here! It is the go-to drug to control and prevent seizures in eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h6)

question: Why is recent rectal surgery considered a strict contraindication for a flatus tube?

options.A: It disrupts healing surgical suture lines and causes injury
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: It permanently damages the anal sphincter muscles
options.D: It causes severe respiratory depression

explanation: Inserting a tube into a freshly operated rectum can tear fragile sutures, cause severe hemorrhage, and damage healing tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: What's the main difference between 'in situ' breast cancer and 'invasive' breast cancer?

options.A: In situ cancer only affects men, while invasive cancer only affects women
options.B: In situ cancer causes severe pain, while invasive cancer is completely painless
options.C: In situ cancer stays confined within the ducts, while invasive cancer spreads to surrounding tissue
options.D: In situ cancer requires chemotherapy, while invasive cancer requires no treatment

explanation: In situ means 'in its place'—it hasn't broken out of the duct yet. Once it breaks through, it's invasive and can travel. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which system in the body pumps out stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline when you face a sudden scare?

options.A: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
options.B: The lymphatic fluid drainage system
options.C: The gastrointestinal digestive tract
options.D: The superficial integumentary system

explanation: It is a big mouthful to say, but the HPA axis is your body's master alarm system for stress. It floods your system with cortisol to get you ready for action! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h4)

question: What makes droplet nuclei so tricky when it comes to spreading infections?

options.A: Blocking the entry of viruses into the upper respiratory tract
options.B: Causing localized skin infections through direct contact
options.C: Settling immediately on nearby surfaces within one meter
options.D: Carrying airborne infectious pathogens over long distances

explanation: Great job thinking about how germs travel! Droplet nuclei are tiny dried-out particles that stay floating in the air for a long time, letting them travel far on air currents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h1)

question: An elderly client living alone cannot walk well enough to go to the local market. What community resource can you suggest?

options.A: A commercial fast-food chain
options.B: A high-intensity exercise gym
options.C: A home-delivered meal program
options.D: An inpatient hospital admission

explanation: Brilliant! Meal-delivery services are a fantastic way to make sure clients with mobility issues still get proper nutrition at home. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h6)

question: What is the name of the economic indicator used to measure a country's total output of goods and services?

options.A: Inflation rate average
options.B: Consumer price index
options.C: Gross domestic product
options.D: National debt ceiling

explanation: Great job! Gross domestic product (GDP) is just the big financial scorecard showing how healthy a nation's overall economy is. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h2)

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient with diabetic foot neuropathy to test bathwater with their elbow instead of their feet?

options.A: Numbness in the feet prevents the patient from accurately sensing water temperature, risking scald burns
options.B: Elbow skin contains specialized sweat glands that neutralize toxic minerals found in tap water
options.C: Hot water causes immediate and permanent paralysis of the small motor nerves in the toes
options.D: The skin on the feet is biologically incapable of absorbing heat evenly compared to the upper body

explanation: Because neuropathy takes away normal feeling in the feet, patients might step into water that's way too hot without realizing it until they get burned. Using the elbow helps keep them safe! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h7)

question: A patient visits the clinic with stomach upset, tension headaches, and poor sleep after getting a major promotion at work. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Symptoms of an acute bacterial gastrointestinal infection
options.B: Early warning signs of a neurodegenerative disorder
options.C: Adverse reaction to routine vaccination
options.D: Physiological and psychological manifestations of acute stress

explanation: Even good life changes can overwhelm the body! These physical aches and sleep troubles are classic signs that stress is taking a toll. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the main goal of disaster mitigation?

options.A: To completely eliminate all natural hazards on earth
options.B: To manage patients only after a disaster has occurred
options.C: To reduce the severity and impact of potential disasters
options.D: To provide immediate funding for post-disaster recovery

explanation: You've got this! Mitigation is all about lessening the damage from hazards that we cannot completely stop. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which hormones primarily drive the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Thyroid hormones and cortisol
options.B: Growth hormone and melatonin
options.C: Estrogens and testosterones
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone are the main chemical drivers of pubertal development. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT checked during a care home regulatory inspection?

options.A: Sanitation and food hygiene practices in the kitchen
options.B: Proper storage and administration of resident medications
options.C: Staff-to-resident ratios on every shift
options.D: Personal investment portfolios of the facility directors

explanation: Well done! Inspectors focus entirely on resident safety, health, and facility standards—not the private finances of management. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why are nurses in such a great position to catch adverse drug reactions early?

options.A: They are legally responsible for manufacturing all hospital drugs
options.B: They maintain close, continuous contact with hospitalized patients
options.C: They perform all laboratory blood chemistry tests
options.D: They set the retail prices for pharmaceuticals in Nigeria

explanation: Because you spend the most time right at the bedside, you are usually the first to notice early physical or mood changes after a patient takes a drug. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h8)

question: Which surgical treatment provides a permanent cure so fibroids never return?

options.A: Uterine artery embolization
options.B: Hormonal birth control
options.C: Myomectomy
options.D: Hysterectomy

explanation: A hysterectomy removes the entire uterus, meaning fibroids have nowhere left to grow. It's the ultimate definitive cure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h6)

question: What is the main job of a receptor in a reflex pathway?

options.A: Contraction of skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Releasing hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Converting physical stimuli into electrical nerve signals
options.D: Processing complex thoughts in the cerebral cortex

explanation: Receptors act like translators, changing physical stuff like heat or touch into the electrical language that nerves can understand. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a core duty expected of a nurse, no matter where they work?

options.A: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.B: Administering prescribed medications safely
options.C: Advocating for the health and safety of patients
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and clinical progress

explanation: Surgeries like brain operations are strictly done by trained surgeons, not nurses, regardless of whether it's a primary clinic or a tertiary hospital! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is a classic, go-to sign of leprosy?

options.A: Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck
options.B: Severe joint pain and morning stiffness
options.C: High fever and generalized body rash
options.D: Definite loss of sensation in a skin patch

explanation: Correct! A pale or reddish skin patch that has completely lost its feeling is a major clue for leprosy. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal way that toxic substances cause a medical emergency?

options.A: Disrupting cellular oxygen use at the tissue level
options.B: Blocking the normal electrical signals of the heart
options.C: Stimulating the production of healthy bone marrow cells
options.D: Causing sudden and profound systemic vasodilation

explanation: Making healthy blood cells in the bone marrow is a good, normal process! Toxins cause harm by damaging systems, not by boosting healthy growth. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h5)

question: What are the smaller building blocks that join together to make proteins?

options.A: Nucleic acids
options.B: Simple sugars
options.C: Amino acids
options.D: Fatty acids

explanation: You can picture proteins like long chains made of individual Lego bricks—and those bricks are amino acids! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) compared to basic health education?

options.A: Promoting and sustaining healthy community practices
options.B: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Writing medical records for hospital filing
options.D: Increasing the number of operating theatres

explanation: You got this! BCC goes beyond just sharing facts—it actively helps communities adopt and stick to healthy habits for the long run. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to talk directly with teenagers during nutrition counselling, rather than only talking to their parents?

options.A: It legally removes parental responsibility for food purchases.
options.B: Teenagers refuse to speak to adults unless parents leave the room.
options.C: It helps teens build personal responsibility for making healthy choices.
options.D: Parents have no influence over what teenagers buy or eat.

explanation: Brilliant thinking! When teens are involved in the conversation, they feel respected and are more likely to actually stick to healthy habits. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h7)

question: What usually happens to your search precision when you broaden your search terms to increase recall?

options.A: Precision increases because the computer works twice as fast
options.B: Precision drops to zero because the system crashes immediately
options.C: Precision stays exactly the same regardless of search terms
options.D: Precision decreases because more irrelevant results get pulled in

explanation: There is a classic inverse relationship between precision and recall; casting a wider net brings in more noise along with the good articles. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why might two people experience the exact same traumatic event, but only one develops PTSD?

options.A: They have different underlying vulnerabilities and coping resources
options.B: The person who stayed healthy must have taken secret vitamins
options.C: Psychological trauma only affects individuals with high blood pressure
options.D: Trauma never causes long-term mental health problems in adults

explanation: Individual differences in genetics, past experiences, and coping skills mean stress affects people differently based on the diathesis-stress model. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which brain chemical helps calm nerve activity and is often out of balance in people with anxiety?

options.A: Histamine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Think of GABA as the brain's natural 'chill pill'! It's our main calming chemical, keeping our nervous system from going into overdrive. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h3)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the ABCDE emergency assessment framework?

options.A: Brain function
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Breathing

explanation: The ABCDE acronym stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, and Exposure. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h2)
